purpose: Treprostinil is used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), which is high blood pressure in the blood vessels of your lungs. It helps you breathe more easily, improves your ability to exercise, and slows down how quickly your condition gets worse. It is not a cure, but it helps manage your symptoms and improve your quality of life.
how_it_works: Your lungs have blood vessels that can become too narrow and stiff with PAH, making your heart work extra hard. Treprostinil works like a natural substance in your body called prostacyclin, which helps relax and widen those blood vessels. This makes it easier for blood to flow through your lungs, reducing the strain on your heart.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, flushing (feeling of warmth or redness), jaw pain, diarrhea, nausea, and feeling lightheaded or dizzy. If given as an injection under the skin or through a vein, pain, redness, or irritation at the injection site is very common. The inhaled form may cause cough, throat irritation, or dizziness.
warnings: Do not stop taking treprostinil suddenly without talking to your doctor — stopping abruptly can cause your condition to get much worse very quickly. Tell your doctor if you have low blood pressure, liver problems, or are pregnant or breastfeeding. If you use the injectable form through a central line (IV), there is a risk of serious bloodstream infections, so keeping the line clean is extremely important. Always carry backup supplies in case your infusion pump or inhaler has a problem.
typical_dosing: Dosing is very individual and is carefully adjusted by your doctor based on how you respond and tolerate the medication. It comes in several forms: a continuous injection under the skin or into a vein (pump), an inhaled form you breathe in several times a day, or an extended-release tablet taken with food. Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it to find the right amount for you.
